In many ways, Vine was the blueprint.

title: feat(notifications): mark all as read when leaving the screen

labels.name: needs-issue
labels.description: PR needs a linked tracking issue

body:
## Summary

- When the user opens notifications (either the standalone `/notifications` route or the Notifications segment inside the inbox) and then leaves, every visible notification is flipped to read and the badge collapses to 0.
- Triggers: bottom-nav tab switch (ShellRoute unmount), Messages/Notifications segment toggle inside `InboxView` (KeyedSubtree swap), and auth flip (pubkey-keyed subtree remount).
- The badge stays at 0 until a genuinely new unread notification arrives — either pushed live via `acceptRealtime` or returned as unread by the next `refresh()`. No change needed on the badge side: `watchUnreadCount()` is already derived from the snapshot.

## Implementation

A small `MarkAllReadOnDispose` stateful wrapper fires `NotificationRepository.markAllAsRead()` once in `dispose()`. The repository already does the optimistic snapshot flip + server write + rollback on failure (the PR #4034 semantics), so the badge cubit and feed bloc recover consistently if the API call fails.

- `mobile/lib/notifications/widgets/mark_all_read_on_dispose.dart` *(new)* — the wrapper.
- `mobile/lib/notifications/widgets/widgets.dart` — export it.
- `mobile/lib/notifications/view/notifications_page.dart` — wrap `NotificationsView`.
- `mobile/lib/notifications/view/inbox_notifications_page.dart` — wrap `_InboxNotificationsScaffold`.

### Why a wrapper instead of a bloc event

The repository's `markAllAsRead()` must outlive the `BlocProvider` being torn down with the route. The repository instance is owned higher up (Riverpod), so dispatching a bloc event in `dispose` would race the bloc's own close. Calling the repository directly from the wrapper sidesteps that.

### Why dispose-on-leave and not on-open

Mark-on-open would hide brand-new notifications the user hadn't actually seen yet (e.g. a relay arrival in the same frame as the open). The existing `notifications_page_test.dart` "does not mark notifications read on open" assertion still pins that contract — only the dispose path was added.

### Shell architecture note

I verified `app_router.dart` uses a plain `ShellRoute`, not `StatefulShellRoute.indexedStack`. That means tab switches via the bottom nav *do* unmount the previous tab's subtree, so `dispose()` is the right trigger. If we later migrate to `StatefulShellRoute`, this would need to be re-wired to a route listener.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter analyze lib/notifications test/notifications` — clean
- [x] `flutter test test/notifications/view/notifications_page_test.dart test/notifications/view/inbox_notifications_page_test.dart test/notifications/widgets/mark_all_read_on_dispose_test.dart` — 19/19 pass
- [x] New `MarkAllReadOnDispose` widget tests cover mounted-no-call, unmount-calls-once, error-swallowing, and child rendering
- [x] New "marks all notifications read when the page is unmounted" test on both `NotificationsPage` and `InboxNotificationsPage`
- [x] Existing "does not mark on open" + "does not fan out across the five filter tabs" assertions still pass
- [ ] Manual: open inbox → notifications segment → tap home → return to inbox → notifications badge should be 0, list rows show read styling
- [ ] Manual: open notifications → background app → foreground → badge state preserved (dispose did not fire)
- [ ] Manual: receive a new like/comment via WS while away from notifications → badge bumps to 1

title: fix(macos): use data protection keychain to stop repeated keychain prompts
body:
Closes #4575

## Summary

- Removes the explicit `useDataProtectionKeyChain: false` override on `MacOsOptions` in `flutterSecureStorageProvider`. The flutter_secure_storage default is now `true`, which uses the modern data protection keychain.
- Items are scoped to the `keychain-access-groups` entitlement (already configured in `DebugProfile.entitlements` and `Release.entitlements` as `\$(AppIdentifierPrefix)\$(CFBundleIdentifier)`) instead of the binary's code signature. Rebuilds no longer trigger the "enter your login keychain password" prompt for every stored item on every fresh build.

## Why

Every `flutter run` / fresh macOS build produces a new code signature. The legacy login keychain scopes ACLs to that signature, so the user gets prompted once per stored item (auth token, nostr key, OAuth tokens, pubkey cache, …) on every rebuild. "Always Allow" only sticks for a single signature. The data protection keychain uses the `keychain-access-groups` entitlement instead, which is stable across signatures.

## Tradeoff

Existing macOS users have credentials in the legacy login keychain. After this change the app reads the data protection keychain and won't find them, so they'll need to sign in again on macOS. iOS, Android, and Linux are unaffected.

## Test plan

- [ ] Fresh `flutter run -d macos` no longer prompts for the login keychain password.
- [ ] Sign in, quit, rebuild, relaunch → still signed in, no keychain prompt.
- [ ] On the first run after the upgrade, the user is prompted to sign in again (expected — see Tradeoff).

title: fix(audio): route extracted audio paths to AudioSourceConfig.file (#4395)
body:
## Problem

Crashlytics issue `e81e2bc1d6713fa5d91e7b15a0950e18` (16 events, 2 users, v1.0.13):

```txt
StateError: Bad state: No host specified in URI ...extracted_audio_xxx.wav
  _HttpClient.getUrl
  AudioClipPlayer._defaultRemoteAudioFileLoader
  AudioClipPlayer.setClip
  AudioTimingCubit._setClippedAudioSource
```

`AudioEvent.url` is overloaded: it contains either network URLs **or** bare absolute file paths (e.g. from `clip_editor_bloc.dart` via `extractAudio(videoPath)`). `AudioTimingCubit` classified everything non-bundled as `.network`; the default remote loader passed the path without scheme validation to `HttpClient.getUrl`.

## Fix

- **`AudioTimingCubit`** (primary): three-way classification in `_setClippedAudioSource`
  - bundled → `AudioSourceConfig.asset`
  - `file://` URI or bare absolute path (starts with `/`) → `AudioSourceConfig.file` (decoded via `Uri.toFilePath()`)
  - otherwise → `AudioSourceConfig.network`

- **`AudioClipPlayer`** (defense-in-depth): `_defaultRemoteAudioFileLoader` now throws `ArgumentError` for non-http(s) schemes instead of silently passing a broken URI to `HttpClient.getUrl`.



Closes #4395

title: feat(recorder/library): clip trash bin with 30-day retention
body:
Closes #4547

## Summary

Replaces the recorder's destructive "delete last clip" gesture with a
two-layer safety net:

1. **Snackbar Undo (5 s)** — taps to the bottom-left button now schedule a
   soft-delete and show a "Clip moved to trash • Undo" snackbar. Undo
   restores the clip to its original tray position.
2. **30-day trash bin** — clips that aren't undone land in a new
   *Recently deleted* screen (accessible from the clips library), where
   they sit for 30 days before auto-purge. Each row offers Restore /
   Delete now, plus a single "Empty trash" action.

Library-tab deletes are routed through the same `softDelete` path so
both surfaces share one delete behavior. Icon swapped from
`arrowCounterClockwise` → `trash` so the affordance reads as
*destructive-but-recoverable* instead of *undo my last tap*.

Motivation: in-app feedback from `723glimmers` — accidentally tapped
"undo" while assembling a brownie-batter compilation and lost a step.
The undo button's icon promised reversibility but the action was a
single-tap, no-confirm, on-disk hard delete with no recovery.

## Architecture

- **Schema:** `clips.deleted_at` (nullable timestamp) + idx_clip_deleted_at.
  All existing read paths now filter `deleted_at IS NULL`.
- **`ClipLibraryService`** split into `softDelete` / `restore` /
  `hardDelete` / `getTrashedClips` / `purgeExpiredTrash`. `softDelete`
  optionally clears `draft_id` so a recorder-trashed clip lands in the
  library on restore rather than a stale session.
- **`ClipManagerNotifier`** tracks the pending deletion in state, commits
  it on `addClip` / `reorderClip` / `clearAll` / dispose so a fresh
  recording never leaks a half-undone state.
- **`ClipsLibraryBloc`** gains four events: `TrashLoadRequested`,
  `RestoreClips`, `HardDeleteClip`, `EmptyTrash`, plus `trashedClips`
  and `lastDeletedClipIds` on state.
- **`purgeExpiredTrash(retention: 30d)`** runs on app startup from
  `app_lifecycle_handler.dart` (best-effort, idempotent).

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter test test/services/clip_library_service_test.dart` — softDelete / restore / hardDelete / purgeExpiredTrash coverage
- [x] `flutter test test/blocs/clips_library` — 64 tests, including state-prop shape after new fields
- [x] `flutter test test/providers/clip_manager_provider_test.dart` — `scheduleDeleteLastClip` smoke
- [x] `flutter test test/widgets/video_recorder` — both recording modes

- [x] `flutter test test/l10n/arb_consistency_test.dart` — new keys allowlisted
- [x] `packages/db_client` migration test — schema add safe

- [ ] Manual: capture-mode tap → snackbar dismiss → clip in *Recently deleted* → Restore → library
- [ ] Manual: classic-mode same flow
- [ ] Manual: trash → Delete now → file gone
- [ ] Manual: trash → Empty trash → all files gone
- [ ] Manual: kill app, relaunch → trashed clips persisted

Eight new keys: `videoRecorderClipUndoLabel` + 7 `libraryTrash*` keys.
Allowlisted in `arb_consistency_test.dart`; translators will pick them
up in the next localization pass. `videoRecorderClipDeletedMessage`

other locales fall back to the prior translation until refreshed.

## Summary
On iOS, the audio recorded during a video recording session gradually increases in volume over time. The issue appears to be triggered specifically when the countdown feature is used before starting the recording.

The audio volume progressively increases throughout the recording — the longer the recording, the louder the audio becomes.

Audio volume should remain consistent and stable throughout the entire recording session.

Source audit context: `origin/main` at commit `1be7b7790` (2026-05-18). This issue extends the [April 2026 simplicity audit](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/blob/main/docs/code-review/issues-simplicity.md) and is filed as a child of #4339 per the [ratification thread](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/issues/4339#issuecomment-4473808375).

## Severity
High

## Problem
`mobile/lib/providers/app_providers.dart` has grown to 2,918 lines and is the #1 merge-conflict hotspot in the repo (114 commits over the last 90 days). It mixes Nostr-key providers, blocklist providers, curated-list state, video-feed wiring, signing adapters, performance adapters, and bridge adapters in a single file with eight section dividers but no boundary enforcement. Adding any new provider — in any domain — forces every contributor to touch the same file, and any non-trivial change ripples conflicts across in-flight feature PRs.

This is distinct from #3336, which addresses the *semantics* of `app_providers` polling. This issue addresses the *structure* — splitting the file itself.

## Evidence
- `mobile/lib/providers/app_providers.dart`: 2,918 lines, 114 commits in the last 90 days (top file by churn).
- Section dividers at lines 473, 993, 1232, 2472, 2553, 2595, 2658 — already domain-grouped in comments, but co-located in one file.
- `BlocklistVersion` class at line 1139, `CuratedListsState` at line 2211, `_AuthServiceBridgeAdapter` at line 2843, `_BlossomAuthAdapter` at line 2876, `_FirebasePerformanceAdapter` at line 2902 — different concerns, same file.
- April 2026 audit baseline: 2,500 lines. Growth: +418 lines (+17%) since the audit.

## Impact
High. Merge-conflict hotspot at #1 by 90-day commit count. The single-file structure forces serialized provider work; any independent feature touching providers stalls behind whatever else is in flight. The eight existing section dividers prove the boundaries already exist conceptually — they just need to become file boundaries.

## Recommended fix
Split by domain into `mobile/lib/providers/`:
- `auth_providers.dart` (Nostr keys, signing adapters)
- `blocklist_providers.dart` (`BlocklistVersion`, blocklist state)
- `curated_lists_providers.dart` (`CuratedListsState`, related)
- `video_providers.dart` (feed/video wiring not already extracted)
- `infrastructure_providers.dart` (Blossom, Firebase performance, bridge adapters)
- `app_providers.dart` becomes a thin re-export barrel during migration

Land one extraction PR per domain, each under ~24h, to keep conflict load on in-flight feature PRs bounded. Migrate behind a re-export barrel so consumer imports don't break across in-flight branches.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `mobile/lib/providers/app_providers.dart` is under 400 lines (re-export barrel only).
- [ ] Each domain provider file is under 800 lines.
- [ ] No provider in a domain file depends on Flutter widgets directly (use repository/service abstractions).
- [ ] Each extraction PR is independently shippable and reverts cleanly.
- [ ] Riverpod codegen still passes; `dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs` produces no diff after the split.

## Related issues
- Parent epic: #4339
- Distinct from #3336 (DI readiness semantics — does not address file size)

title: refactor(async): use .timeout() in BackgroundActivityManager (#4517)
body:
Closes #4517

## Summary

First single-file slice of #4517's production `Future.delayed` cleanup.

Replaces the hand-rolled `Future.any([Future(fn), Future.delayed(...)])` timeout in `BackgroundActivityManager._performImmediateBackgroundActions` with the proper `.timeout()` API. **The change is API hygiene, not behavior** — see the "Honest accounting" section below for what does and doesn't change at runtime.

Also extracts the 1-second grace window into `_suspendGracePeriod` so the intent (and its current defensive-only status) is named at the field rather than implied at the call site.

## Diff shape

```dart
// Before
await Future.any([
  Future(service.onAppBackgrounded),
  Future.delayed(const Duration(seconds: 1)),
]);
// → silent timeout, no exception, no log

// After
await Future(service.onAppBackgrounded).timeout(_suspendGracePeriod);
// → explicit TimeoutException, caught + logged via Log.warning
```

## Honest accounting

`BackgroundAwareService.onAppBackgrounded` returns **`void`**, and the two in-tree implementations are purely synchronous:

- `AuthService.onAppBackgrounded`: `_bunkerSigner?.pause()` — sync, no `unawaited()`
- `AnalyticsService.onAppBackgrounded`: `_isInBackground = true` — sync, no `unawaited()`

This means **`Future(voidFn)` completes in one microtask in every case that exists today**, and `.timeout()` cannot fire. The original `Future.any` bound never fired either. The timeout wrapper is purely defensive against a future widening of the interface to `FutureOr<void>` (or a service that starts blocking the microtask chain).

I considered deleting the timeout wrapper entirely as dead-by-construction code (per "don't design for hypothetical future requirements"), but kept it because the file already structured this way and removing it is bigger than #4517's mandate. Happy to file a follow-up issue to simplify this once #4339 Wave 2 stabilizes if reviewer prefers.

The refactor's concrete benefits:
- Removes one `Future.delayed` call site (the #4517 mandate).
- Names `_suspendGracePeriod` as a constant with explicit defensive-only doc.
- If the interface is ever widened, the timeout starts producing `TimeoutException` with a distinct log line, rather than silently swallowing the bound.

## Tests

Updated `background_activity_manager_test.dart`:
- Refreshed the inline comment on `'should register and notify services'` to describe the new `.timeout()` chain shape (still microtask → completion).
- **Added regression test**: `'isolates a throwing service so remaining services still get notified'`. Pins the cross-service failure-isolation contract — a `_ThrowingBackgroundService` raises synchronously inside the same suspend pass as the healthy `TestBackgroundService`, and the test asserts the throw is caught while the sibling still gets notified.

Disclosure: this test passes against both the old `Future.any` code and the new `.timeout()` code — it pins a previously-untested invariant of the loop, not a new behavior introduced by this PR. Per #4517 acceptance, it is event-queue-drained (`pumpEventQueue`), not sleep-based.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — clean
- [x] `dart format` — clean
- [x] `flutter test test/services/background_activity_manager_test.dart` — **6 passed**

## Inventory delta against #4517

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Files in `mobile/lib/` with `Future.delayed` | 18 | **17** |
| Call sites in `mobile/lib/` (per #4517 body) | 30 | **29** |

`grep -rln "Future\.delayed" mobile/lib --include="*.dart" | grep -v l10n/generated | wc -l` is the canonical CI guard mandated by #4517 acceptance criterion 3; that guard is not part of this PR.

## Reviewer

Per the established Wave 3 hygiene pattern (#4339), only @NotThatKindOfDrLiz added once CI returned green.

title: techdebt(async): remove remaining production Future.delayed call sites

labels.name: simplicity
labels.description: Duplication, oversized files, and unnecessary complexity

body:
Source audit context: `origin/main` at commit `1be7b7790` (2026-05-18). Filed as a child of #4339 per the [ratification thread](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/issues/4339#issuecomment-4473808375). Supersedes closed-incomplete #3582.

## Severity
Medium

## Problem
`Future.delayed` is used in production app code for UI-timing coordination and ad-hoc retry/backoff. Closed issue #3582 ("Remove Future.delayed calls in app code (22 files)") was closed without the work landing — multiple production call sites remain. CLAUDE.md explicitly forbids `Future.delayed` for UI timing (use `AnimatedSwitcher`, `AnimationController`, stream listeners instead).

This issue supersedes #3582 with the scope corrected per the [#4339 ratification](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/issues/4339#issuecomment-4473808375): scoped to remaining *production* call sites only (helper docs / comments excluded). Live inventory in this issue's body, updated as call sites land.

## Evidence
- Current count: 30 `Future.delayed` call sites across 18 production files in `mobile/lib/` (excluding generated/l10n).
- Forbidden by `.claude/rules/code_style.md`: "No `Future.delayed()` for UI timing."
- Forbidden by Nostr async rules in `CLAUDE.md`: "Avoid introducing arbitrary `Future.delayed()` calls in app code; prefer explicit async coordination."
- Closed predecessor: #3582 (closed-as-completed but work not landed).
- Existing leaf already tracked: #3604 (`Cancel orphaned Future.delayed in VideoFeedItem`) — keep open as a concrete first slice; this issue tracks the broader cleanup.

## Impact
Low-Medium. Each `Future.delayed` site is an arbitrary timing assumption that breaks under jank, throttling, or test `fakeAsync`. Cumulative effect: flaky tests, brittle UI timing, orphaned futures outliving disposed widgets.

## Recommended fix
For each call site, pick one of:
1. UI timing: replace with `AnimatedSwitcher` / `AnimationController` / `TickerProvider`.
2. Retry/backoff: extract to a typed retry policy class (e.g. `ExponentialBackoff`) with cancellation support.
3. Stream coalescing: replace with a proper `StreamTransformer` (debounce / throttle / buffer).

Land per-file, not as a megafile rewrite. Each PR removes one or a small group of related call sites and adds a regression test asserting the timing-free behavior.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `grep -rln "Future\.delayed" mobile/lib --include="*.dart" | grep -v l10n/generated | wc -l` returns 0.
- [ ] Each removed call site has a behavioral test (not a sleep-based test) that asserts the new coordination works.
- [ ] CI introduces a guard (lint or grep-based check) preventing reintroduction.

## Related
- Parent epic: #4339
- Supersedes closed-incomplete: #3582
- Concrete first slice: #3604 (VideoFeedItem-specific case)

title: task(notifications): run post-fix regression sweep across unread, routing, dedupe, and push flows
body:
## Summary
After the recent notifications stabilization work, we still need one deliberate regression and QA sweep across the highest-risk user paths so we can close the epic with confidence.

This issue is for end-to-end validation of notification behavior across unread state, tap routing, realtime-vs-REST dedupe, push registration, cold start delivery, and layout behavior under larger device font settings.

## Assignee
`@Chardot`

## Weekly Priority
`P1`

## Parent
- `#4200`

## Dependencies
- `#4206`
- `#4207`

## Related Completed Work
- `#4204`
- `#4205`
- `#4264`
- `#4208`
- PR `#4162`

## Scope
- verify unread convergence across badge, inbox list, and effective content-open paths
- verify tap routing for likes, comments, replies, mentions, and reposts
- verify WS-first -> REST-later dedupe behavior for standalone and grouped notifications
- verify cold-start push registration and delivery after signer/session readiness changes
- verify signed-out -> signed-in and account-switch transitions do not leave stale registration or stale unread state
- verify notification row layout, sizing, and alignment under larger device font settings

## Test Matrix
- fresh cold launch with an already-signed-in account
- signed-out -> signed-in transition
- account switch between two known accounts
- notification arrives over WS first, then later through REST refresh/pagination
- notification opened from inbox list
- notification opened from push tap on cold start
- larger accessibility/device font sizes on notification rows
- iOS device coverage for push behavior
- Android device coverage for push behavior if available this week

## Acceptance Criteria
- no known unread-state divergence remains across badge, list, and opened content
- no known tap-target regression remains for core notification kinds
- no duplicate logical notification appears when WS and REST deliver the same event in different orders
- cold-start push registration and push-open behavior are reliable after session readiness changes
- signed-out, signed-in, and account-switch transitions leave notification state explicit and correct
- row layout remains visually correct at larger device font sizes
- any discovered failures are either fixed in linked follow-up PRs/issues or explicitly documented before the epic is closed

## Done When
- the notifications subgroup agrees the high-risk paths have been exercised deliberately
- remaining failures, if any, are linked from this issue and from `#4200`
- if no failures remain, this issue is closed with a concise verification summary

## Coordination
Coordinate with the notifications subgroup while running this sweep:
- `@dcadenas` for push registration / cold-start delivery
- `@realmeylisdev` for unread-state and dedupe verification
- `@untreu2` for routing verification

Please link any regressions found back to `#4200` rather than opening ungrouped bug shards unless the breakage is clearly independent.
